questions.def: Use 'the' to refer to a specific, unique person or thing.
questions.question: She is ___ only person who understood my joke.

questions.def: Use 'the' with comparatives to show correlation.
questions.question: ___ more you study, the better you will do.

questions.def: Omit 'a' before uncountable nouns used in a general sense.
questions.question: A reason for his success is hard work.

questions.def: Use 'an' before a vowel sound; 'expert' is singular countable.
questions.question: He's ___ (expert) in this field.

questions.def: No article needed when visiting prison for its intended purpose.
questions.question: They went to ___ prison to visit their father.

questions.def: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound, so use 'an'.
questions.question: He is ___ honest man.

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'university' despite the initial vowel letter.
questions.question: She is a university student studying medicine.

questions.def: Use 'the' before unique positions like 'head of the department'.
questions.question: She is ___ (head) of the department.

questions.def: Use 'the' to refer to a group of people (the rich).
questions.question: ___ rich should pay more taxes.

questions.def: Use 'a' in exclamatory sentences with singular countable nouns.
questions.question: What ___ beautiful day!

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'European' because it sounds like /j/.
questions.question: She is ___ (European) woman.

questions.def: Use 'the' before musical instruments.
questions.question: He plays ___ guitar very well.

questions.def: Use 'the' when referring to a unique item.
questions.question: She is ___ only child.

questions.def: Use 'an' before 'hour' because the 'h' is silent.
questions.question: I need a hour to finish this.

questions.def: Use 'an' before words starting with a vowel sound.
questions.question: He is ___ (architect).

questions.def: Use 'the' before superlative adjectives.
questions.question: She is ___ best student in the class.

questions.def: Use 'the' with 'outskirts'.
questions.question: He lives on ___ outskirts of town.

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'university' because it sounds like /j/.
questions.question: She is ___ (university) professor.

questions.def: Use 'the' to refer to a specific, unique position.
questions.question: He is ___ CEO of the company.

questions.def: Use 'the' before plural country names (United States).
questions.question: She went to ___ United States.

questions.def: Use 'the' with most to show superlative.
questions.question: This is a most interesting book I have read.

questions.def: Use 'an' before a vowel sound; 'engineer' is singular countable.
questions.question: He is ___ (engineer).

questions.def: Use 'the' before names of planets (Earth).
questions.question: ___ Earth revolves around the sun.

questions.def: Use 'the' when referring to a specific thing.
questions.question: She is ___ only person I trust.

questions.def: Use 'an' before 'employee' as it begins with vowel sound.
questions.question: He is a employee at the company.

questions.def: Use 'an' because 'honorary' starts with a vowel sound.
questions.question: She is ___ (honorary) member.

questions.def: Use 'the' before superlative adjectives.
questions.question: They are ___ happiest people I know.

questions.def: Use 'a' before United Nations as a general reference.
questions.question: She is ___ United Nations representative.

questions.def: Use 'the' for specific meetings known to both speaker and listener.
questions.question: ___ meeting has been scheduled for next Tuesday.

questions.def: Use 'an' before vowel sounds; engineer starts with a vowel sound.
questions.question: He's studying to become ___ engineer.
